items.title: EU leaders ‘light-years away’ on agreeing budget at summit, warns Giorgia Meloni – Europe live
items.summary:
A number of leaders hope to agree to a budget before consequential elections around the continent

The Danish prime minister, Mette Frederiksen, has acknowledged that leaders remain “very far apart,” agreeing with Germany’s Merz that the current proposal is not going to work.

“The budget is too large and not sufficiently future-oriented,” she said, calling for more work on competitiveness, defence and security.

Continue reading...
items.t: EU leaders brace for tough talks on budget and Ukraine – Europe live

items.title: Egypt: 31 people killed in Cairo after fuel truck overturns
items.summary: A fire broke out on a busy highway in Egypt’s capital, Cairo, on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people after a fuel truck reportedly overturned. The suspected driver was arrested on Thursday, according to Egypt’s public prosecutor’s office.
items.t: Egypt: 31 people killed in Cairo after fuel truck overturns

items.title: Alleged Islamic State group propagandist Emily Konig on trial in France
items.summary: Accused of being one of the Islamic State group's most active French propagandists, Emily Konig went on trial in Paris on Thursday. Originally from Brittany, Konig spent a decade in Syria before returning to France in 2022. She is charged with criminal association with a terrorist organisation and faces up to 30 years in prison if convicted. FRANCE 24's Luke Shrago is following the trial in Paris and joins us to explain the defence's strategy.
items.t: Alleged Islamic State group propagandist Emily Konig on trial in France

items.title: Fuel tanker explosion kills 31 on Egyptian highway
items.summary: A massive fire killed 31 people in Egypt after a speeding driver allegedly crashed into a fuel tanker truck.
items.t: Fuel tanker explosion kills 31 on Egyptian highway

items.title: French media publish fresh claims of far-right leader Bardella's 'anti-Semitic torrent'
items.summary: PRESS REVIEW – Thursday, November 26: French media outlets Mediapart and Le Monde publish an additional trove of messages purporting to show far-right leader Jordan Bardella's rampant anti-Semitic thoughts as a young member of the party in 2013. Also: France holds the first trial of a female jihadist, Émilie König. Kilmar Abrego Garcia, once the face of Donald Trump's brutal mass deportations, arrives in Spain. Plus: we find out why the rich world is in the midst of a "sex recession."
items.t: French media publish fresh claims of far-right leader Bardella's 'anti-Semitic torrent'

items.title: France: Senior officials investigated over suspected leaks to far-right National Rally
items.summary: Two senior figures in France have been caught up in an investigation into suspected leaks to the far-right National Rally. The prefect of the Loiret and former top official at the Interior Ministry, Hugues Moutouh, has been removed from his post after being suspected of passing on confidential information about investigations. A deputy prosecutor in Paris, who was found at the party's headquarters during a police search, is now also under administrative inquiry
items.t: France: Senior officials investigated over suspected leaks to far-right National Rally

items.title: EU Budget talks: France seeks to protect Common Agricultural Policy subsidies
items.summary: Leaders from EU countries are meeting in Brussels on Thursday and Friday for another round of talks on the EU's next multi-year budget. For France, the main aim of the negotiations is to prevent a reduction in the funding allocated to the Common Agricultural Policy, a subsidy vital for French agriculture – a position Macron made clear in a meeting with farmers unions in Paris on Wednesday.
items.t: EU Budget talks: France seeks to protect Common Agricultural Policy subsidies

items.title: Trump unveils new tariffs on 14 trade partners over 'unfair' industrial capacity
items.summary: US President Donald Trump fired a new tariff salvo on Wednesday on 14 major trading partners including China, Japan and the European Union, undeterred in his protectionist push by the losses his Republican Party suffered in US midterm elections. His administration proposed new maximum potential rates of 20% to 40% to counter excess industrial capacity that it says these countries are promoting.
items.t: Trump unveils new tariffs on 14 trade partners over 'unfair' industrial capacity

items.title: 'King tide' waves batter California coast, soaking San Francisco
items.summary: Massive waves carried on king tides battered California's coast Wednesday, prompting evacuations and soaking San Francisco, but sparing feared mass disruptions to Thanksgiving holiday travel. San Francisco already recorded its highest November water levels in more than 40 years on Tuesday morning, according to the National Weather Service.
items.t: 'King tide' waves batter California coast, soaking San Francisco

items.title: Ministers ‘fail to make case’ for Heathrow third runway, MPs report says
items.summary:
Transport committee says policy papers show expanding airport would fall short of pledges on economy and climate

Ministers have “failed to make the case” for a third runway at Heathrow, according to a damning report by MPs.

The Commons transport committee said on Thursday that the detailed policy papers laid out by the government showed that expanding the London airport would fall short of pledges on the economy and climate.

Continue reading...
items.t: Ministers ‘fail to make case’ for Heathrow third runway, MPs report says

items.title: Oil prices inch back up as Iran and the Houthis escalate threats
items.summary: Increased fighting between Iran's Houthi allies and Saudi Arabia and Tehran's unrelenting threats in the Strait of Hormuz appear to be reversing weeks of oil price declines.
items.t: Iran denounces U.S. use of AI during war

items.title: 'Sacré sel': France's love of salt
items.summary: We take a look at a salt scandal that is rocking the UK, after Maldon sea salt was found to come, in part, from rock salt imported from Germany. We also discuss France's relationship to salt (le sel) and the different kinds in France, from fleur de sel to sel gris. Finally, we look at French history and expressions about salt.
items.t: 'Sacré sel': France's love of salt

items.title: Norse Atlantic Airways suspends all flights as it makes urgent funding plea
items.summary:
Norwegian airline says its finances are ‘critical’ and it will file for bankruptcy if it cannot secure short-term backing

  • Business live – latest updates

Norse Atlantic Airways has suspended all flights and said it will file for bankruptcy if it cannot secure short-term financing urgently.

The Norwegian airline, which operates long-haul flights around the world including from London Gatwick and the US to Europe and Asia, announced it was on the brink on Thursday morning, a day after warning that its finances were “critical”.

Continue reading...
items.t: Norse Atlantic Airways suspends all flights as it makes urgent funding plea

items.title: Older Australians suffering under Labor’s ‘botched’ aged care at home program, inquiry finds
items.summary:
The Support at Home system has ‘baffling’ bureaucracy and ‘rations and denies care’, says Greens chair of Senate inquiry

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Many older Australians are dying before they can access home support, paying exorbitant fees, and being pushed into hospitals and residential care before they are ready because of a flawed federal government aged care program, a Senate inquiry has found.

The inquiry is examining the impact of the Support at Home program, which launched in November 2025 and has been plagued by complaints of making care harder to access and more expensive. The inquiry was due to finish in November, but has been extended for a further year after receiving almost 300 submissions.

Continue reading...
items.t: Older Australians suffering under Labor’s ‘botched’ aged care at home program, inquiry finds

items.title: Russia-Ukraine war extends to the Baltic and the Mediterranean
items.summary: By attacking Russian vessels around the world, Kyiv is trying to up the pressure on Moscow and also sending out signals to its Western allies. What is the impact on global maritime trade?
items.t: Russia-Ukraine war extends to the Baltic and the Mediterranean

items.title: New defence laws could have ‘significant’ implications for human rights, Labor-led inquiry finds
items.summary:
Anthony Albanese defends laws and calls criticism ‘nonsense’ and ‘conspiracy theories’ from far left and far right

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

New powers allowing defence officials to use lethal force against suspected trespassers into designated zones could have “significant” human rights implications, a Labor-chaired inquiry has warned.

The committee also raised concerns about a lack of requirements to ensure anyone detained under the new laws had access to fresh drinking water and humane conditions. It noted the broad and extensive changes could capture unwitting members of the public who stumble on to a declared defence security zone that has not been publicised.

Continue reading...
items.t: New defence laws could have ‘significant’ implications for human rights, Labor-led inquiry finds

items.title: Details of two treaties at heart of Andy Burnham’s EU reset to be published
items.summary:
Government also to publish bill that will enact EU deals as Tories and Reform hit out over 10-year termination clause

  • Europe live – latest updates

  • Business live – latest updates

Details of two treaties at the heart of Andy Burnham’s post-Brexit reset plans will be published on Thursday alongside the bill that will implement the changes into UK law.

The treaties signed by the UK and the European Union at last week’s summit will have a 10-year termination clause that would mean if one party were to end the agreement, they would have to pay to rebuild border checks infrastructure, the BBC reported on Thursday.

Continue reading...
items.t: Details of two treaties at heart of Andy Burnham’s EU reset to be published

items.title: Le Pen's top ally Bardella faces fresh allegations of anti-semitic comments
items.summary: French investigative outlet Mediapart on Thursday published extracts from private conversations in which far-right leader Jordan Bardella allegedly made anti-semitic remarks as a teenager, prompting fresh accusations that he has denied.
items.t: Le Pen's top ally Bardella faces fresh allegations of anti-semitic comments

items.title: 'We are not fighting culture, we fight to end FGM: It's a human rights violation of women and girls'
items.summary: “We fight to end FGM because it is a human rights violation of women and girls. We are not fighting culture.” Caroline Lagat, Legal Advisor at Equality Now’s Africa office in Nairobi, discusses the challenges of ending female genital mutilation (FGM) and child marriage. She points to insufficient funding, conflicting marriage laws and growing community resistance to campaigns against FGM. While acknowledging some progress, Lagat calls on the government to be "the face of the campaign to end FGM and child marriage.”
items.t: 'We are not fighting culture, we fight to end FGM: It's a human rights violation of women and girls'

items.title: Injury-hit PSG drop first points of Champions League campaign against Roma
items.summary: After kicking off their Champions League title defence with four consecutive wins, Luis Enrique's men were held to a draw at home by the Italian side Roma. Real Madrid are now two points clear at the top of the standings.
items.t: Injury-hit PSG drop first points of Champions League campaign against Roma

items.title: Huge explosion at oil depot in Bangkok sends fireball into sky
items.summary: An explosion at an oil depot in Bangkok sent a large fireball and thick black smoke into the sky, journalists said Thursday, as local authorities urged people nearby to evacuate.
items.t: Huge explosion at oil depot in Bangkok sends fireball into sky

items.title: Coalition to privatise Melbourne sewage plants and sell state land and renewables if it wins election
items.summary:
Liberal and Nationals’ policy costings also reveal ‘air rights’ between Richmond train station and MCG would be sold

  • Victorian election 2026 guide: what you need to know

  • Confused about who to vote for? Check the parties’ key promises and policies

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

A Victorian Coalition government would privatise two sewage plants and sell off state-owned land, renewable energy assets and the “air rights” between Richmond train station and the Melbourne Cricket Ground if elected.

The opposition leader, Jess Wilson, released the Liberal and Nationals’ pre-election policy costings on Thursday, just two days before the state election and after more than 1.5 million Victorians have already cast their vote.

Continue reading...
items.t: Coalition would privatise Melbourne’s sewage treatment while selling state-owned land and renewables to fund Victorian election promises

items.title: Aid cuts to Taliban-ruled Afghanistan further curb women's access to healthcare, education and food
items.summary: Having lived and worked in Afghanistan for seven years, photojournalist Élise Blanchard offers an intimate account of what daily life is like for Afghan women today. Joining Genie Godula on the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, she explains how restrictions vary across the country, depending on where women live, their families and the local enforcement of Taliban decrees. She stresses the need to maintain access to healthcare, primary education and food, pointing to severe cuts in humanitarian assistance by the US and EU.
items.t: Aid cuts to Taliban-ruled Afghanistan further curb women's access to healthcare, education and food

items.title: 'Unacceptable': China, EU among major economies against new US tariffs
items.summary: China, the European Union and other major trading partners on Thursday criticised new US tariffs of up to 20 percent proposed by US President Donald Trump after a probe into alleged global overcapacity, raising the prospect of fresh trade tensions with allies and rivals alike.
items.t: 'Unacceptable': China, EU among major economies against new US tariffs

items.title: EU leaders face showdown over Ukraine funding as divisions deepen
items.summary: European Union leaders on Thursday are set to tackle deep divisions as they meet in Brussels to discuss the bloc's long-term budget in Brussels, which includes a proposed €45 billion loan to keep Ukraine funded through 2027.
items.t: EU leaders face showdown over Ukraine funding as divisions deepen

items.title: ‘Are they all turncoats?’: Barnaby Joyce says voters are turning to One Nation – and Liberals like Blyth can too
items.summary:
South Australian senator Leah Blyth labels One Nation the ‘only party with the bold ideas needed to turn this country around’

  • Follow our Australia politics live blog for latest updates

  • Get our daily political email, free app or daily news podcast

Leah Blyth, federal Liberal senator for South Australia, has defected to One Nation, blindsiding former Coalition colleagues who called her a “turncoat” and raising further scrutiny of chaos inside the opposition.

Blyth, a shadow assistant minister on Angus Taylor’s frontbench, said in a statement announcing her move that she did not believe the Coalition was capable of opposing the Albanese government.

Sign up for Guardian Australia’s Politics, really newsletter here

Continue reading...
items.t: ‘Are they all turncoats?’: Barnaby Joyce says voters are turning to One Nation – and Liberals like Blyth can too

items.title: Senior Liberal slams Blyth in email to members, saying ‘you gave her your trust, she threw it away’ – as it happened
items.summary:
• Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Pauline Hanson has released a statement this morning welcoming South Australian senator Leah Blyth to her party.

Blyth is the second high-profile federal defection from the Coalition to One Nation – after Barnaby Joyce.

Senator Blyth will be One Nation’s first South Australian Senator and will build on One Nation’s expanding support within the state.

My team and I are delighted to welcome Senator Blyth to sit in the Senate with One Nation.

We are facing at the next election clearly a coalition of the Liberals, Nationals and One Nation, with all the baggage that each of these parties brings to the table. They’re all anti-worker, they’re all extreme … this demonstrates, I think, more disunity in the Liberal party under Angus Taylor.
items.t: Australian politics live: Canavan calls Blyth a ‘turncoat’ after One Nation defection; Bowen says forces ‘infected’ Cop31

items.title: Iraqi court sentences 8 French nationals to life in prison for IS group membership
items.summary: An Iraqi court sentenced eight French nationals to life in prison and two others to 15 years on Thursday for joining the Islamic State group, as Baghdad steps up prosecutions of thousands of alleged jihadists transferred from Syria.
items.t: Iraqi court to sentence 20 French nationals for IS group membership

items.title: How Chinese companies circumvent chips sanctions in Southeast Asia
items.summary: High-tech AI chips are hard to get in China because of US restrictions. To get around this, Chinese companies often use offshore computing capacity, particularly in Southeast Asia. The US is also trying to stop it.
items.t: How Chinese companies circumvent chips sanctions in Southeast Asia

items.title: Trump tariff threat ‘unacceptable’, says Brazil, as China denounces levies as baseless
items.summary:
Brazil indignant about proposed tariffs on sugar and aircraft, while Beijing says new levies amount to ‘political manipulation’

  • Trump proposing new tariffs on 14 partners including China and EU

Brazil has said it will not bend to the new US tariff “threat” and China accused Washington of “political manipulation” in the wake of Donald Trump’s latest economic salvo against 14 major trading partners.

Brazil’s government said on Wednesday: “Brazil will not yield to this type of threat”, adding in its statement that the “unilateral decision constitutes an unacceptable action within the framework of the ongoing bilateral negotiating process”.

Continue reading...
items.t: Trump tariff threat ‘unacceptable’, says Brazil, as China denounces levies as baseless

items.title: 'It’s really outrageous': Women face violence in the streets and 'what we see online is even worse'
items.summary: On International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, FRANCE 24's François Picard is pleased to welcome back Choralyne Dumésnil, an attorney practising in Paris and California, to discuss misogyny, sexual violence, cyberbullying and the challenges victims face in seeking justice. "There's always that stigma when you lodge a complaint. You get questioned, you get cross-examined," notes François Picard. Despite efforts to raise awareness, Dumésnil sees little significant change in society.
items.t: 'It’s really outrageous': Women face violence in the streets and 'what we see online is even worse'

items.title: Can Rassvet, 'Russia's Starlink' change the course of the war in Ukraine?
items.summary: SpaceX's US Starlink satellite system has played a key role in countering the Russian military in Ukraine, but now a Russian counterpart is under development. What could this mean for Ukraine in future?
items.t: Can Rassvet, 'Russia's Starlink' change the course of the war in Ukraine?

items.title: Live: EU leaders meet in Brussels amid division over Ukraine funding
items.summary: EU leaders are set to clash in Brussels on Thursday over a proposed €45 billion loan to fund Ukraine in 2027, with Germany pressing members to contribute and others seeking exemption. A day earlier, US President Donald Trump and NATO chief Mark Rutte urged Russia not to escalate its war with Ukraine after talks in Florida. Follow our liveblog for all the latest updates.
items.t: Live: Trump, NATO chief urge Moscow to not 'expand' Ukraine war

items.title: ‘Trapped in grief’: wife of Japanese journalist detained by Russia pleads for his release
items.summary:
Yuki Imai being held in Moscow on allegations he conducted ‘espionage’ while working for a newspaper in Sakhalin island in Russia’s far east

The wife of a Japanese journalist who has been detained in Russia for more than a month on suspicion of spying has issued an emotive appeal for his release.

Yuki Imai, a reporter for the Hokkaido Shimbun, was arrested in mid-October as he was preparing to return to Japan from a two-year assignment at the Japanese newspaper’s bureau in the city of Yuzhno-Sakhalinsk, on the island of Sakhalin in Russia’s far east.

Continue reading...
items.t: ‘Trapped in grief’: wife of Japanese journalist detained by Russia pleads for his release

items.title: UK to invest £9.5m in Ukraine windfarm to bolster war-hit energy system
items.summary:
Project capable of powering 300,000 homes, with Britain having offered more than £770m to rebuild energy sector

Britain will add to its multimillion pound investments in rebuilding Ukraine’s energy system by funding a windfarm project capable of powering 300,000 Ukrainian households.

Ed Miliband, the UK foreign secretary, said Britain would invest £9.5m to build a 200 megawatt windfarm in an undisclosed location to bolster Ukraine’s energy reserves as its war with Russia approaches the five-year mark.

Continue reading...
items.t: UK to invest £9.5m in Ukraine windfarm to bolster war-hit energy system

items.title: US authorises SpaceX to launch up to one million satellites for orbital data centres
items.summary: The US Federal Communications Commission has approved SpaceX's plan to deploy up to one million satellites to build data centres in orbit, giving Elon Musk's company a major foothold in the industry. The authorisation runs through 2040, as tech firms race to move computing infrastructure into space despite significant technical hurdles.
items.t: US authorizes SpaceX to launch up to one million satellites for orbital data centers

items.title: At least 31 killed in Cairo fire after fuel truck overturns on busy highway
items.summary: At least 31 people were killed and 15 injured when a fuel truck overturned and burst into flames on a busy highway in Cairo on Wednesday, engulfing nearby vehicles, Egyptian authorities said.

items.title: Powerful US storm forces historic postponement of New York's Thanksgiving Day Parade
items.summary: A powerful storm forecast to bring fierce winds and heavy rain to the northeastern United States has forced the unprecedented postponement of the city's 100th annual Thanksgiving Day Parade, with the event rescheduled for Saturday. Officials warned that Thursday's conditions could bring down tree limbs and power lines, while posing a safety risk to the parade's giant balloons and the crowds below.
items.t: Powerful US storm forces historic postponement of New York's Thanksgiving Day Parade

items.title: At least 31 killed as fuel tanker crash ignites large fire on Cairo highway
items.summary:
Blaze on ring road surrounding Egyptian capital injures at least 21 people and leaves cars and motorcycles charred

A crash involving a fuel tanker ignited a huge fire on a highway surrounding Cairo on Wednesday, killing at least 31 people, Egyptian authorities said.

The blaze on the ring road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, also injured at least 21 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, according to the latest figures released by the health ministry.

items.title: All hostages rescued after Colombian security forces storm supermarket, police say
items.summary:
Unclear if ‘hostage-taker’ who was killed may have been a hostage as daylong siege in Cartagena shopping centre ends

Colombian police have stormed a supermarket in one of the country’s most popular tourist cities, ending a daylong siege in which all the hostages were freed and one man police described as a hostage-taker was killed.

Abelardo de la Espriella, the far-right president, travelled to the Caribbean port city of Cartagena to follow the final hours of negotiations and the tactical assault, in which special forces officers broke through blocked entrances and detonated stun grenades.

items.title: Lululemon founder stuns Canadian women’s leadership conference with sexist comments
items.summary:
Chip Wilson said men importing brides from Thailand was due to women waiting too long to have children

The controversial founder of Lululemon suggested women in Canada are having too few children and this could lead some men to bring in brides from Thailand, in remarks that stunned audience members at a women’s leadership conference.

Chip Wilson, who built the Vancouver yoga-wear startup into a global athleisure empire, was a featured speaker at the Leadership Forum in Calgary earlier this week, an event organized by Axis Connects to advance women in leadership. The organization says it aims to create space for “candid conversations about the barriers women face both in business and society”.

items.title: China sends first foreign astronaut to ISS rival as it globalises space operations
items.summary:
Muhammad Zeeshan Ali – the first Pakistani to reach orbit – greeted with Chinese ‘space handshake’ at Tiangong station

China has flown the first foreign astronaut to its Tiangong space station, starting what it says will be the globalisation of its space operations as the US-led International Space Station (ISS) enters its final years of operation.

Floating through a hatch to enter Tiangong, Pakistan’s Muhammad Zeeshan Ali grinned broadly as he was embraced by the onboard crew in what China’s space agency called the country’s first foreign “space handshake”.

items.title: Swiss tourist killed and British and Americans injured by elephants in Cameroon
items.summary:
Alain Throo, insurance executive based in London, reportedly gored and later died on hike near Mount Cameroon national park

A Swiss tourist has been killed and British and American tourists have been injured when a group of hikers encountered a herd of elephants in Cameroon.

The group of six tourists, four British, one Swiss and one American, accompanied by local guides, were hiking near the village of Bakingili in the south of the Mount Cameroon national park on 19 November, on a path used by elephants to access a nearby lake, when they encountered the herd of about 15 animals, according to media reports.

items.title: UK embassy in Japan warns of rise in drink spiking and credit card fraud at Tokyo bars

Social media campaign fronted by British rapper Shao Dow advises tourists not to let their guard down

The British embassy in Tokyo has launched a social media campaign warning visitors to exercise caution after a rise in cases of drink-spiking and credit card fraud against tourists in the Japanese capital.

items.title: Sri Lankan asylum seeker killed himself after being sent by UK to Eswatini
items.summary:
Kishanth Peramalya was denied entry due to sexual assault convictions and sent to Africa where he had no connections

The UK sent a Sri Lankan asylum seeker who had been convicted of sexual assault to Eswatini, a southern African country to which he had no connection and where he killed himself.

Kishanth Peramalya was part of a group that set sail from India hoping to reach Canada and claim asylum there. The boat was rescued by the Royal Navy in October 2021 when it got into difficulty and brought to Diego Garcia in the remote British Indian Ocean Territory, which hosts a US-UK military base.

Continue reading...
items.t: Sri Lankan asylum seeker killed himself after being sent by UK to Africa

items.title: China misusing Interpol to target dissidents, says leading UK lawyer
items.summary:
Concerns over Beijing’s use of ‘red notices’ as Hong Kong prepares to host police organisation’s general assembly

China is misusing Interpol to target and silence dissidents, a leading British lawyer has claimed, as Hong Kong prepares to host the police organisation’s general assembly for the first time.

Ben Keith, a specialist in “red notices” - the Interpol system under which national authorities are requested to locate and detain suspects - said he was working on five cases involving China making questionable requests through Interpol.

items.t: China misusing Interpol to target dissidents, says leading UK lawyer

items.title: Canada says it ‘does not report to the US’ after Pentagon criticizes military spending
items.summary:
Scathing US document memo supposedly ‘atrophied’ defence capabilities of its northern neighbour

Canada is a “sovereign nation” that does not “report” to the United States, the country’s defense minister said after the Pentagon released a scathing memo that criticized the supposedly “atrophied” defence capabilities of its northern neighbour.

The document, released on Tuesday, said Canada had “yet to make the hard decisions and tradeoffs” necessary to meet previous defence spending pledges and become a “credible partner in the defense of our shared continent”.

items.title: More than 300 Russians killed as Moscow props up Mali’s junta, leaked data reveals
items.summary:
Exclusive: Records list 349 deaths in three years in Mali and also shed light on Russia’s military activity elsewhere in Africa

When the attack on Kidal began before dawn on 25 April this year, the Russian fighters were caught off guard. Within the first hour, checkpoints on the outskirts of the remote desert city nestled among the rocky hills of northern Mali had fallen to the insurgents, who pushed towards the police station where fierce fighting erupted.

“Everything was happening at once. Explosions were going off all around us, people were shouting,” recalled a former member of Russia’s Africa Corps who was stationed in Mali at the time and spoke on condition of anonymity. “Nobody knew where the enemy was coming from.”

Continue reading...
items.t: More than 300 Russians killed as Moscow props up Mali’s junta, leaked data reveals

items.title: Ukraine confirms it used naval drones to strike two Russian ships off Libya

Ukraine’s security service says seven drones were launched from mothership in operation that sank Merkury warship

Ukraine has confirmed it deployed naval drones in strikes on two Russian vessels off Libya on Sunday, including one that sank the corvette Merkury, one of Russia’s newest vessels.

Ukraine’s security service, the SBU, said seven domestically made naval drones were launched from a mothership in the operation, which Volodymyr Zelenskyy described as “exemplary”.
